picks.headline: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson needs thumb surgery, will go on IR TRENDING NFL Week 8 updates NFL Winners & Losers College Fantasy Waiver Wire F1 Mexico City GP updates Williams earns MVP honors NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joey Bray Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The one game standing between the 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and their bye week is their most consequential yet, as they are set to take on the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. When the ball is kicked, it will be exactly a month to the day since Cleveland took the first game between the teams on Thursday Night Football. However, the Steelers have rattled off three straight wins since then. The winner of this game will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North heading into the second half of the regular season. With both teams coming off wins and identical records, FanDuel Sportsbook gives the Pittsburgh Steelers the slight edge as a 3.5-point favorite over Cleveland. This is as close to a "must-win" game in the middle of the season for the Steelers as we will ever see. With all of that being said, here are some predictions based around my favorite prop bets of the weekend. Germie Bernard over 43.5 receiving yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Wide receiver Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates the first down in the fourth quarter at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images This number is ridiculously low because the rookie receiver will be one of, if not the most targeted pass catchers on the entire team on Sunday. Last time these two teams met, Bernard got barely any playing time, but that gives him the chance to take advantage of a group that hasn't seen what he can do yet. In their first matchup, Pittsburgh had two receivers go over this total. I'm not letting last game scare me, as the Steelers controlled the clock running the football, leading to limited opportunities for any receiver. It would be a shock to see no receiver have more than three catches for the second week in a row. Bernard is a volume receiver that the Steelers will need to rely on to get open and break some tackles against their tough man defense. Rico Dowdle gets over 70 scrimmage yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Ifeatu Melifonwu #5 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackles Rico Dowdle #13 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ever since running back Rico Dowdle has returned to the lineup from his toe injury, he has looked significantly more efficient with the ball in his hands. Sure, the improved offensive line helps, but Dowdle is going to continue to earn more runs in the offense with his numbers improving. Last week, the veteran back averaged a season-high 4.6 yards per carry. Dowdle also hauled in six passes, good for the most on the team, for 45 yards. It was a more even share of the opportunities for the Steelers running backs, as Dowdle had 16 touches compared to Jaylen Warren's 21. Dowdle is the change of pace back in the Steelers offense, but is one that they will continue to use quite a bit as he gets healthier. Warren's breakout doesn't mean that Dowdle won't be involved in the offense. In fact, I think what we saw against New Orleans is what we can expect from Dowdle for the rest of the season. With the browns struggles to defend the run, both backs could be in for a big day on Sunday. Darnell Washington continues dominance with a touchdown TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Darnell Washington #80 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a pass from Aaron Rodgers #8 during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers' six-foot-seven tight end has already set career highs in total touchdowns this season. His increased usage in the red zone is something Steelers fans have been begging to see for years now. Last week, Washington dunked on Saints defensive back Kool-Aid McKinstry as he snatched the ball out of the air from four yards out for the Steelers' only touchdown in Paris. The tight end has caught a touchdown pass in two consecutive games, and I have a hard time seeing that trend stopping against Cleveland given his continued usage in the red zone. Washington also scored against the Browns in their first matchup a month ago. It almost makes too much sense to see Washington in the end zone again on Sunday. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North. Final score prediction: Steelers 35, Browns 24 This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game

picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lamar Jackson needs thumb surgery, will go on IR TRENDING NFL Week 8 updates NFL Winners & Losers College Fantasy Waiver Wire F1 Mexico City GP updates Williams earns MVP honors Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game. Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball. Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa. It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win. Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17 Garrett Chapman (3-4) The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive. The Buccaneer defense is solid, and it will be a difficult test on the road for an offense that hasn't shown it can consistently be a steady unit. Atlanta has a chance to take over the top spot in the NFC South on Sunday, but it won't happen just yet. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. However, the winner of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' Week 8 battle with the Atlanta Falcons will likely determine who is the favorite to win the division. At 2-5, the Bucs have been left for dead more than once this season. However, their 43-13 annihilation of the first-place Carolina Panthers has them right back in the thick of the division race. Now only one game out of first place, Tampa's season has officially risen from the dead. If the Bucs can beat the 3-4 Falcons on Sunday, they will be only half a game behind the Panthers, who fell to 3-4 with their loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday. However, securing a victory over Atlanta will be no easy task. The Falcons are marching into Raymond James Stadium on a high note after their 29-20 win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers last week. This crucial NFC South showdown will have a big say in who takes the division crown this season and features two teams that have walked similar paths through the season's first seven weeks. The Bucs and Falcons both had high expectations coming into the season. Both teams have talented rosters and were hoping to break free of their recent curse of mediocrity. Like the Bucs, the Falcons fell flat coming out of the gate. After two straight losses to start the season, including an embarrassing 34-3 home defeat to the Panthers in Week 2, Atlanta looked like the league's worst team. However, those losses came with starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and backup Tua Tagovailoa both injured. The Falcons were forced to start third-string Cooper Rush in the first two games before he was benched for Jack Strand. Penix returned in Week 3 and led Atlanta to a dominant 35-14 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, followed by a 45-24 thrashing of the New Orleans Saints on the road in Week 4. In those victories, plus last week's triumph over the 49ers, the Falcons have looked like a legitimate playoff team. The Bucs have also looked like a bottom-feeder for much of the season. However, in their demolition of the Panthers and a Week 5 road upset over the Dallas Cowboys , the Bucs have also looked like a playoff team. Both teams have taken turns as Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde this season. Which version of each team will we see on Sunday? In my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory , I highlighted the need for Tampa's defense to contain superstar Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson and to find a way to stop tight end Kyle Pitts, who has been a Buc-killer his entire career. If the Bucs can do both, they have a great chance to earn their third victory of the season. If not, it could be a long afternoon for the home team. The Bucs must also give their own star RB, Bucky Irving, a healthy workload to control the clock and keep the potent Atlanta offense on the sidelines. If Irving gets 20+ touches and Baker Mayfield takes care of the ball in his second game back from a three-game absence with a broken thumb, the offense should have success. I believe the Bucs' defense, which has been strong all year, will slow the Falcons offense just enough for Tampa to get its second straight victory. I think a late Penix interception will seal the game for the Bucs. Prediction: Bucs 30, Falcons 24

home.blurb: Backup running back Brian Robinson Jr. had already missed Week Seven against the San Francisco 49ers with a hamstring injury. That injury lingers, and he is out this week. Khalil Herbert will continue to back up starting running back Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was downgraded to out with a hamstring injury. With veteran safety Jessie Bates III , veteran defensive back Sydney Brown, and young safety Xavier Watts making the middle of the field a tough place to play for opposing offenses, Bowman Jr. has enough reinforcements to heal. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out again with a foot injury. Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. have been a one-two punch for Tampa this year, with almost identical stats. The main difference is that Egbuka has the touchdowns, with two this season. We will see how much that affects Tampa's offense on Sunday. Backup running back Kenny Gainwell and offensive tackle Luke Goedeke are both questionable and could also miss Sunday's game, hindering the offense. Last week's game plan was to lean on the run game, which will be harder without the backup running back and with an offensive lineman out. On paper, the Falcons have the advantage heading into Sunday's game. But you never know how these things play out. It bodes well for the Falcons to take advantage and win on Sunday, as it would give them control of the NFC South. Charlie Disturco Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:26 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts (2-5) and Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) will meet in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Jaguars are 10.5-point favorites over the Colts on the spread, with the total set at over/under 46.5 points. Jacksonville is a -520 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Indianapolis is a +400 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Colts vs Jaguars prediction and player prop pick for today's game. Colts vs Jaguars pick: Bhayshul Tuten Over 64.5 Rushing Yards (-111) My Jaguars vs. Colts best bet is Bhayshul Tuten to record over 64.5 rushing yards. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Colts vs Jaguars NFL Odds Colts vs Jaguars Spread : Colts +10.5 (-122), Jaguars -10.5 (+100) Colts vs Jaguars Total : over/under 45.5 (-106o / -114u) Colts vs Jaguars Moneyline : Colts +400, Jaguars -520 Colts vs Jaguars Preview for NFL Week 8 Indianapolis Colts Preview: Everything for Sale The fire sale is officially on in Indianapolis. Following a third consecutive loss, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson ( Seahawks ) and DeForest Buckner ( 49ers ). Josh Downs has also requested a trade, while all eyes have shifted toward the team's prized possession: superstar running back Jonathan Taylor . For now, there are no expected changes at quarterback. Colts head coach Shane Steichen doubled down on Daniel Jones , who threw for just 108 yards last week. The veteran quarterback has struggled mightily this season, throwing more interceptions (7) than touchdowns (4) while posting a career-low completion rate of 59.6%. There is some positive news for Indianapolis, however. Tyler Warren is expected to return to the starting lineup after missing two games with a groin injury. The same goes for Sauce Gardner , while Downs will also suit up despite his trade request. Warren's presence is a must for a Colts receiving room that includes 34-year-old Keenan Allen and journeyman Laquon Treadwell . The question remains: Can the Colts weather the storm and put up a fight against their division rival? The biggest question is how the offensive line will hold up against a formidable Jaguars defense. Indianapolis ranks around league average in rushing yards per game, but those numbers came with Nelson anchoring the offensive line. Taylor is already averaging a career-low 4.2 yards per carry, and losing another key piece up front certainly won't help. The Colts defense has its own issues, ranking in the bottom 10 in points allowed per game and 11th in rushing yards allowed (124.4). Rush defense is definitely Indy's Achilles' heel on the defensive end, ranking 29th in rushing EPA allowed. The pass defense, however, has been surprisingly solid. Indianapolis hasn't allowed a wide receiver room to reach 100 receiving yards since Week 4, while opposing receivers are averaging just 10 receptions per game. Jacksonville Jaguars Preview: Bhayshul Tuten Due for Breakout Game It was a much-needed bye week for the Jaguars, who are coming off two London games filled with late-game theatrics. Jacksonville's defense has been its strong suit this season. Outside of the Texans (34 points), no team has scored more than 17 against this talented unit. The Jaguars rank No. 1 in rushing yards allowed per game (72.2) but have struggled mightily against the pass, ranking 30th while surrendering 274 yards per game. Ultimately, Jacksonville's success will hinge on Trevor Lawrence and the offense finding another gear. The Jaguars are around league average in total offensive production and have maintained a near 50-50 split between the passing and running games. I'd be surprised if Jacksonville's ground game doesn't start to take off soon as Bhayshul Tuten is on the verge of a breakout. The explosive running back possesses elite speed and has already shown the ability to rip off chunk plays. Unfortunately, several of those big gains have been wiped away by holding penalties. Still, Tuten has rushed for at least 65 yards in five of his six games this season. I've been waiting for this offense to take the next step, and there are plenty of weapons to make it happen. Outside of Tuten, Jacksonville has a talented receiving corps led by Parker Washington . We also saw Travis Hunter become more involved offensively before the bye, recording four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown. That increased usage is a trend I expect to continue in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr. has also been the subject of trade speculation ahead of the upcoming deadline. He was benched for the second half against Houston and hasn't recorded a catch in either of Jacksonville's last two games, making his involvement worth watching. One situation worth monitoring is Jakobi Meyers , who enters Sunday questionable after missing Friday's practice with hamstring and ankle injuries. Thomas would likely be relied on to step up in his absence. Another development I've highlighted previously is Jacksonville's increased use of two-tight-end sets. Brenton Strange has been nothing short of excellent, but the emergence of Nate Boerkircher could be just as important moving forward. The second-round pick played a career-high 55% of the snaps before the bye, and I expect his workload to consistently settle in the 50–60% range. Colts vs Jaguars Picks, Betting Analysis I hinted at it earlier, but I expect the Jaguars' ground game to take off. To me, it's a matter of when, not if. Tuten is PFF's No. 1-ranked running back and ranks among the league's best in yards after contact per carry. He draws a Colts run defense that has struggled all season and will be without one of its most important defensive players in Buckner. With Jacksonville entering this matchup as a double-digit favorite, I expect the Jaguars to control possession and lean heavily on the ground game. That should mean a healthy workload for Tuten. Coming off a bye, Tuten should be fresh and ready to take advantage of a spiraling Colts squad. Don't be surprised if he finally breaks the 100-yard rushing mark in this one. home.blurb: The Jaguars officially ruled defensive back Antonio Johnson out for Sunday's game vs. the Colts , with the fourth-year safety set to miss the AFC South battle due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 6 in London against the Houston Texans. Johnson has not practiced for the Jaguars this week, being listed as a non-particpant in all three practices. With Johnson officially out on Sunday, the Jaguars will more than likely turn to safety Kaevon Merriweather to start against the Colts, but who exactly is the veteran safety and what does he bring to the table? Jaguars-Colts Friday Injury Report: 1 Player Must Step Up in Antonio Johnson's Absence Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will be without a big piece of their defense against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Jaguars have seen their safety group get hit with injuries at different points this season, and Merriweather has been one veteran who has helped steady the waters. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. This included 14 games with the Buccaneers in 2024 when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen was the team's offensive coordinator. “Need Kaevon to continue to step up and evolve. But being with him in Tampa, he was a guy that really helped on teams and played his tail off there but was also able to step in and he started, I think, like eight games for us that year in ‘24 at safety. The game wasn't too big for him," Coen said on Friday. Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. home.blurb: With that said, health in this game is going to be critical, so let's take a look at the final injury report for the Chargers with players who are out, questionable, and on track to play. Additionally, Awosika, Thompson, and Leonard did not practice all week so head coach Jim Harbaugh and the coaching staff knew that they would be without those three players as well, which like James should not have affected the game plan too much. Lastly, for Mack to be available is not a surprise at all, as he was simply resting, and as a veteran, that is fairly normal for Mack so he should be a full go against the Rams' offensive line on Sunday. So, when the game starts on Sunday, it will be interesting to see if the Chargers can come out and have a full 60-minute performance to earn their first win of the year or if the Chargers' struggles will continue and lead to a Rams win as well as the Chargers falling to 0-7. Replicating that performance is going to be much easier said than done in the rematch, however, especially with Andy Reid's team hitting the road. Denver seems to be finding its stride just a little bit, although a win over the Arizona Cardinals won't convince anyone that the reigning division champions are all the way back. The winner of Sunday's tilt could generate some serious momentum in the AFC West race as the season approaches its midpoint. What gives in the afternoon window of play? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 8 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: For the second week in a row, I'm expecting a low-scoring game. This time, however, I think the Chiefs will find the end zone. Kansas City just needs enough from Rashee Rice and his fellow pass catchers to allow Kenneth Walker to have opportunities similar to the ones he took advantage of in Week 1. The final inactives list will be massive for both teams, but I expect the Chiefs to escape Denver with a narrow win. Jordan Foote: Getting wideout Rashee Rice back in the fold for this one is huge. Given that Xavier Worthy's come back down to earth, Travis Kelce is banged up and Kenneth Walker III has finally looked human, having a formidable weapon on offense is paramount. On the other side of the ball, missing cornerback Mansoor Delane will hurt, but being minus L'Jarius Sneed might just be an addition-by-subtraction scenario. Expect a one-score game that is far from the prettiest, albeit with Kansas City still doing enough to complete the sweep of Denver and maintain first place in the AFC West. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are reeling after an ugly loss to Seattle in prime time last week. It’s difficult to imagine the offense looking any more inept than it did a week ago when it mustered just one field goal all night. The Broncos’ defense isn’t quite as dominant as Seattle’s but still is a formidable unit. With that said, we saw who the better team was when these two sides met in Week 1. Denver has been winning in spite of Bo Nix’s play, not because of it, and the KC coaching staff has to have stressed the importance of a game in which it could lose the first-place lead in the AFC West. Tyler Brown: This feels like a tighter game than Week 1, but the Chiefs' strengths match up well against those of the Broncos. Denver will be desperate with the divisional stakes swinging so heavily. With Jonathan Cooper lined up opposite Nik Bonitto, the Broncos have a better edge-rush pairing than they did in September, which puts the Chiefs’ tackle situation under real stress if it ends up in too many obvious dropback situations. The Broncos may perform better this go-around, but the matchup tilts toward the Chiefs. Denver’s rushing defense ranks 28th and leads the league in missed tackles, which is exactly the situation Kenneth Walker thrives in. Getting Rashee Rice back is a bigger deal than it may sound, because it gives Patrick Mahomes another reliable weapon and it lets Xavier Worthy and the rest of the group settle into their roles. On the other side, Denver is 30th in total offense and 25th in scoring, and Nix has struggled when pressured, especially against the blitz. If Steve Spagnuolo gets creative and some pass rushers outside of George Karlaftis step up, that is another major Chiefs advantage. The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires. Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time? Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Denver has weathered a very tough schedule to open the 2026 season, beating the Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Arizona Cardinals to begin the year at 5-2. While Denver’s offense has not been great (22nd in EPA/Play), the defense is a top-10 unit once again. Nix and Co. seemed to find a rhythm in a win over Arizona in Week 7, and they’ll look to carry that into a home date against Mahomes and the one-loss Chiefs. Kansas City dominated Denver at home in Week 1, winning by three touchdowns, but it’s coming off a shaky performance against the Seattle Seahawks in a loss in Week 7. The Chiefs are still 5-1 this season, but they scored just three points in their last game and failed to reach the red zone on a single possession. Will a Denver defense that has been red hot in recent weeks be able to slow down Kenneth Walker III and this Chiefs attack? All season long, the SI Betting team has been sharing final score predictions as a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, we’ve hit a few exact scores, which can make for a fun long shot bet from time to time during the season. With a ton at stake in this matchup – including first place in the AFC West – here’s a look at my prediction for the Chiefs vs. Broncos rematch in Week 8. Chiefs vs. Broncos Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs -1.5 (-105) Broncos +1.5 (-115) Broncos: -102 40.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been much movement in the odds for this game, as the Chiefs opened as 1.5-point road favorites even with their loss to Seattle on Sunday night. The total has dropped a point from 41.5 to 40.5, and it’s worth noting that the UNDER hit in this matchup in Week 1 with the Chiefs winning 31-10. Chiefs vs. Broncos Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every single game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s buying the Chiefs on the road in this AFC West showdown: The Broncos' offensive issues and Bo Nix's play are going to haunt them against a good defense sooner rather than later. Their offense is 23rd in EPA per play and 29th in success rate, making them one of the worst offenses in the league through the first seven weeks. Now they take on a Chiefs team that has been impressive defensively, ranking fifth in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. I'd like to see the Chiefs' offense lean on the run game even more moving forward, as they rank in the top three in every offensive rushing metric. They can use that weapon against a Broncos defense that has struggled to stop the run compared to recent seasons. They're 27th in opponent rush EPA. If the Chiefs can lean on their run game and continue to play good defense, they're going to get the road win and cover the short spread. A lot of this game comes down to two things: Do you believe in the Denver offense after a strong Week 7? And, how much stock do you put into Kansas City’s Week 1 win at home? The Broncos are still just 22nd in EPA/Play, 29th in success rate and 26th in yards per play on offense. That isn’t going to cut it against Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III, especially since Denver is allowing 4.6 yards per carry on defense. These teams are No. 5 (Kansas City) and No. 6 (Denver) in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball, and the UNDER has hit in the majority of both of their games. I expect another low-scoring affair with the Chiefs’ offense ultimately being the better unit on Sunday. away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. away.headline: Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns
away.blurb: The Chiefs downgraded rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to out with a shoulder injury, and the Chiefs have also placed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve, according a report from Charean Williams of Pro Football Talk and multiple other outlets. Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Lamar Jackson needs thumb surgery, will go on IR Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns Bob McCullough Sun, November 1, 2026 at 12:24 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs secondary just got a lot thinner, but they're getting a key receiver back for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos. On offense, the news is about receiver Rashee Rice, who will be back in the lineup according to a report from Nate Taylor of ESPN. Rice will be returning from a hamstring injury he sustained against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. Rice was able to participate in every practice this week, per reports, and he currently has 13 receptions on 16 targets for 190 yards and a touchdown. As for the two cornerbacks, Delane is the more serious injury by far. The rookie was Kansas City's top draft choice with the No. 6 pick in the draft, and his shoulder has been an issue since OTAs. He wore a non-contact jersey for most of the summer, but Delane was able to get back on the field for the Chiefs' opener against the Denver Broncos, and he had a big interception in Kansas City's 31-10 romp. But Delane has been on and off the injury report for weeks now with this same issue, so the news isn't exactly surprising. What was surprising, though, was coach Andy Reid revealing that the injury was a hairline fracture of his scapula. His stat line at the moment includes 27 tackles, an interception and five passes defended in five games this season. Sneed's situation is very different. He returned to Kansas City during the summer after a failed stint with the Tennessee Titans. His injury designation was personal/knee, but the personal part of this is new if there's anything substantial to it. Sneed played well early, but he was badly exposed in Kansas City's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night. The Seahawks picked on Sneed for most of the night, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba especially had some strong moments against the former Chiefs star. The Chiefs have also signed cornerback Melvin Smith to the active roster from the practice squad, and they activated defensive end Tyreke Smith from the practice squad to the game-day roster. Kansas City is 5-1 going into Sunday's contest at Denver, which is 5-2. with the two teams battling for the lead in the AFC West.

home.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
home.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. More news : Jonathan Taylor Trade Talks Heat Up as Colts Change Their Stance Delane, the Chiefs’ sixth overall pick, initially injured his right shoulder during the offseason and aggravated it in the season opener against Denver. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. More news : NFL to Review New Allegations Against Packers Star Josh Jacobs More news : Jets Send Clear Message on Garrett Wilson Amid Trade Buzz Losing both players is a tough blow to Kansas City’s secondary, particularly against a division rival that’s found its rhythm over the past few weeks. Delane has become the Chiefs’ primary shutdown corner, while Sneed provides experience and flexibility to move around the defensive backfield. Kristian Fulton and Nohl Williams should likely see expanded roles in the meantime. The timing is also less than ideal considering the Chiefs’ upcoming schedule. After the Broncos on Sunday, Kansas City will host the Jets before traveling to face the Falcons and hosting the Cardinals. home.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). home.headline: Is Jaylen Waddle playing today? Broncos injury report as WR listed as questionable
home.blurb: Waddle didn't practice on Wednesday and put in only limited work on Thursday and Friday, leaving him with a questionable tag entering the weekend. But the news on Sunday morning is positive: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports that the former Alabama star is "trending in the right direction to play" in Week 8. That's not a completely definitive answer, of course, but at this point it would be a surprise if Waddle didn't at least suit up against Kansas City. The phrasing there does leave at least some wiggle room, though. And given that this is a chest injury that Waddle has been battling for some time now, one that he reaggravated last weekend seriously enough to not only take him out of the game but hold him back in practice this week, it's fair to wonder how much he'll be able to offer Denver's offense. home.headline: Denver Broncos Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
home.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Denver Broncos have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. Surtain suffered his ankle injury during Denver's Week 4 game against the 49ers and has been sidelined since. The All-Pro cornerback was a limited participant throughout Week 7 but returned to full participation this week. He carries no injury designation and is expected to return against Kansas City, which is a huge boost for the Broncos' defense. Hufanga, on the other hand, suffered his ankle injury during Denver's Week 5 victory over the Chargers and has missed the Broncos' last two games. He didn't practice this week and has been ruled out for Sunday's game. The Broncos have ruled out two players for Sunday's game and listed four others as questionable. Along with Hufanga, running back RJ Harvey has been ruled out after suffering a knee injury during the week. Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday as a limited participant but did not practice Friday. Defensive lineman Zach Allen, offensive tackle Garett Bolles, safety Brandon Jones and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle are all listed as questionable for Sunday's game. All four were limited participants Friday, and their availability will be determined closer to game day. We'll see if the Broncos can get back to full health for their huge divisional matchup against the Chiefs, but the biggest news for Denver this week is the return of Surtain, who immediately strengthens a Denver secondary that relies heavily on man-to-man coverage. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. away.blurb: Barkley returned to practice on Friday — albeit in a limited capacity — after being listed under did not participate on Wednesday and Thursday. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. But the team should protect him from himself and sit him down if he’s not nearly healthy enough to play and remain in the game. Which is reasonable to think that’s the case considering he wasn’t even able to fully participate in a practice this week! While overcompensating for his hamstring injury, Barkley injured his back on his first rushing attempt in Week 7 and then played sparingly through obvious discomfort the rest of the game. What’s the point of that? What if he gets further injured? That’s not only a setback as it relates to this season, which very well might be cooked anyway, but potentially long-term as well. It could also prevent teams from making offers not only ahead of the NFL trade deadline but in the offseason, too. Even if you’re not of the mind he should be traded at any point, you should want him healthy for next year! I just think playing him is a short-sighted decision with much more downside than upside. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks did not practice this week ahead of their second straight game missed; the Eagles will once again be without their top two wide receivers. With Covey also out, the Eagles only have four healthy wide-outs on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Against the Cowboys last week, Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles WR while Lemon was right behind him. Despite this, Cooper only saw three targets while Lemon saw eight. Bennett fully participated in practice all week. He’s still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him from IR in order for him to play on Sunday. They’ll need to open a roster spot to do so. Nolan Smith is notably set to return after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. Michael Carter II is also set to return after missing the Eagles’ last two games. Hunt and Ojomo will play but they were limited in practice all week. They’re clearly not 100%. On October 14, the Eagles opened Bennett’s 21-day practice window to return from IR. home.blurb: Out: DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring) Questionable: Jakorian Bennett (knee) “I was really excited about Elijah throughout camp and then he got dinged up in camp and just really glad to have him back. Eagles injury update: Saquon Barkley returns to practice – NBC Sports Philadelphia Eagles Eagles running back Saquon Barkley returned to practice on Friday afternoon and will play on Sunday. By Dave Zangaro • Published October 30, 2026 • Updated on October 30, 2026 at 4:16 pm Saquon Barkley is good to go against the Commanders on Sunday night. After missing the first two days of the week, Barkley returned to practice on Friday afternoon and does not have a game status entering this game. He's expected to play. Barkley (hamstring/back) said he will need to manage his injuries throughout the course of the game with a plan set forth from the Eagles’ training staff. Basically, he doesn’t want his body to lock up. "One day, I’m not going to be playing football," Barkley said. "Whenever that is and I look back, I don’t want to look back and be like, ‘I could have gave it a chance and I didn’t.’ Kind of what I live by. So I’m going to just keep recovering, being smart. home.blurb: Treylon Burks has been downgraded in the team's latest injury report , per ESPN's John Keim. After being limited on Wednesday, Burks did not participate on Thursday due to a foot injury. With the Eagles' season going off the rails after five straight losses , this is a great matchup for Jayden Daniels and the Washington offense to punish the Philly pass defense. But if Burks misses out, other Commanders receivers will need to make up for his absence. In his fifth year in the league, the 26-year-old Burks is on course to surpass his debut season with the Commanders last year. Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery. Those ranges are general medical guidance, not a diagnosis of Monangai. Four weeks and three missed games fit the Grade 2 range. That timeline is typical for an injury that required a specialist and a boot, while milder sprains resolve faster and higher-graded ones linger longer. Chicago has kept Monangai off IR, which requires a minimum four-game absence, because the team expected a shorter timeline. Johnson has called him week-to-week and "trending in the right direction," he said, according to Sports Illustrated .
